overview: Score updates go to SQL (source of truth) and ZINCRBY on Redis. Top-N via ZREVRANGE, own rank via ZREVRANK. Daily boards are separate keys with TTL.

estimation.assumption: Illustrative board: 10M members at 100 B of index state each.
estimation.calculation: 10,000,000 × 100 B ≈ 1 GB before allocator and skip-list overhead.
estimation.result: Real sorted-set memory is higher and must be measured.
estimation.implication: One Redis board has a memory and write limit; shard by score range only when measurements require it.

components.purpose: One ZSET per board; shard by score bucket past ~100M members

components.purpose: Source of truth; rebuild ZSETs from here
components.rationale: Choose keys and indexes from the documented access patterns; replicas provide availability, not conflict-free arbitrary writes.

accessPatterns: Apply a uniquely identified score event; rebuild the serving index.
constraints: Dedup event_id and persist before updating derived ranking state.
relationships: RankIndex materializes the committed score; event/version checks prevent duplicate increments.

accessPatterns: Top-N, player rank, and nearby players.
constraints: One member per player per board. Bucket movement must update counts and directory consistently.
relationships: board_id/player_id members derive from PlayerScore and can be rebuilt after cache loss.

apiDetails.rationale: Authenticate game servers and dedup eventId; clients must not arbitrarily assign scores.
Read the serving sorted sets; document lag if an asynchronous index is used.
A sharded rank needs counts of higher score buckets plus the rank within the player bucket.

steps.title: Game client → LB → Leaderboard Service → Scores DB
steps.explanation: Authenticate a trusted scorer and dedup event_id in the durable score transaction.

steps.title: Leaderboard Service → Redis sorted sets
steps.explanation: Apply the committed score version; reconcile any failed dual write from a durable outbox.

steps.title: Game client → LB → Leaderboard Service → Redis sorted sets
steps.explanation: Use sorted-set top-N or reverse rank; define tie ordering and daily-board expiration.

failureCases.scenario: Score commits but the ranking index update is lost
failureCases.handling: Replay a durable outbox/event log using score versions. Reads may temporarily lag; rebuild Redis from authoritative scores rather than losing results.

alternatives: Use a single sorted-set shard while the board fits measured memory/write limits. Use score-range shards beyond those limits, accepting versioned cross-bucket moves and count-based global rank calculations.
